quote: The technique developed here will be applied to the production of ultra-pure NaI(Tl) detectors for the COSINE-200 experiment.
We expect to use this technique for the fabrication of detectors for the next-generation, COSINE-200 phase of the experiment.
Straws with diameter less than 5 mm are necessary to handle the expected particle rates at the higher beam intensity.

To cope with this, the baseline for a new readout structure will be the reduction of the shaping time to the minimum possible of about 28 ns (the transceiver output has a risetime of about 20 ns which adds to the time constants of the shaper) with a reduction of the amplitude of about 40%, and subsequent digitization at 160 MHz, which is above the Nyquist limit, but which could help in identifying superposition of pulses looking at the width of the pulse.
